summary: Prayoon Mererk works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Delhi (~1981–1985), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Margaret Chatterjee and Mahesh Tiwary.

Prods Oktor Skjærvø is a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Oslo (~1970–1981) and Dr. habil. at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1981–1984), later becoming Aga Khan Professor at Harvard University in 1991.

Projit Bihari Mukharji specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Kolkata, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and SOAS University of London, and held appointments at Newcastle University, McMaster University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Ashoka University.
Pulinbihari Chakravarti was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Jogendranath Vedantatirtha and Satkari Mookerjee. He served as Curator of Manuscripts at the Asiatic Society.

Purushottama Bilimoria, a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, studied under Shivesh Thakur and completed his PhD at La Trobe University (~1983). He has held posts at Deakin University, the University of Melbourne, UC Berkeley, Stony Brook, and Columbia University.
Pyi Phyo Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at King's College London (~2009–2014) and served there as a postdoctoral research fellow around 2014.
Pál Miklós was a scholar in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1946–1950) and Peking University (~1950–1954), and later taught Lilla Russell-Smith.

Péter-Dániel Szántó specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Balliol College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and has held posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Oxford, and All Souls College.

Qian Lin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol under Rupert Gethin, and the University of Washington (PhD 2004–2015) under doctoral supervisor Collett Cox.

Qiang Ning is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who studied under Wu Hung, Irene Winter, and John M. Rosenfield. He worked at Dunhuang Academy and taught at Yale, the University of Michigan, and San Diego State.

Qichao Liang worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied under Kang Youwei (~1890–1898) and at National Tsing Hua University, later holding a post at Tsinghua University (~1925–1929).

Qing Duan was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University and the University of Hamburg, and served as a professor at Peking University from ~1987 to 2022.

Qingying Chen was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology who studied at Qinghai Normal University, Qinghai University for Nationalities, and Minzu University of China. He held posts at Southwest Minzu University, Minzu University of China, and China Tibetology Research Center.

Qingzhi Zhu is a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Peking University (~1999–2011) and held a professorship at The Education University of Hong Kong around 2011.
Qinni Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (~2006–2009) under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin.
Qiwen Xiao is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University (~2010–2013) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.
R. Balasubramanian was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras (~1980–1988).

R. Gordon Wasson was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Columbia University and the London School of Economics, and held posts with the American Expeditionary Forces, several publications, Guaranty Trust Company, and J.P. Morgan & Co.

R. Keller Kimbrough specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shigekatsu Minobe and held posts at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture and the University of Colorado Boulder (~2004).
R. N. Gadre was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and at Savitribai Phule Pune University.
